title: The Knight
subtitle: The L-shaped jumper that ignores walls.

steps.say: The knight is the trickiest piece in chess. It moves in an 'L': two squares one way, then one square sideways. From d4 it can reach these eight squares — and nothing can block its path, because it jumps!
Watch — even on a crowded board, knights hop right over everyone.

autoMoves.say: The knight leaps over its own pawns — no other piece can do that on move one.
And onward to a strong central square. Knights love the center: more squares to jump to.

steps.prompt: Capture the black pawn with your knight.
hints: Count the L: two squares up, one square over.
From d4, the knight reaches e6 in one jump.

line.say: That's the L-shape! Two up, one right — pawn captured.

steps.wrongSay: Remember the L: two squares in one direction, then one square sideways.
steps.successSay: The L-shape will feel natural very soon. Keep jumping!

steps.prompt: A knight's tour! Capture all three pawns, one jump at a time.
hints: Not every pawn is reachable right away — pick the one an L-move actually hits.
From d4 you can capture on c6 or f3 first. From either, the e5 pawn comes next.

sequenceGoal.say: Hop! Now line up the next L.

steps.wrongSay: That's not a legal knight capture. Trace the L carefully: 2 + 1.
steps.successSay: A real knight's tour! You're starting to see the L-shapes without counting.

steps.prompt: Your knight can capture two different pawns — but one is protected. Take the free one!
hints: Look at the f7 pawn — what is it defending?
e6 is guarded by f7. The c6 pawn has no protection at all.

line.say: Correct — c6 was free. The e6 pawn was bait: f7 would have recaptured.

rejections.say: fxe6! The f7 pawn was guarding e6. A knight is worth about three pawns — don't trade it for one.

steps.wrongSay: There's a capture available on two squares — figure out which pawn nobody defends.
steps.successSay: Sharp eyes. Knights and pawns trade at three-to-one — never forget the exchange rate.

steps.prompt: The legendary smothered mate — checkmate in one move!
hints: The black king is completely walled in by his own rook and pawns. Only a jumping piece can finish him.
Which L-jump lands the knight next to the king with check?

line.say: Smothered mate! The king's own pieces block every escape — only a knight, attacking over the wall, could deliver this.

rejections.say: No check — and the king just breathes on. Find the square where the knight attacks h8 directly.

steps.wrongSay: Not mate. The knight must land where its L attacks h8 itself.
steps.successSay: The smothered mate — one of the most beautiful patterns in chess, and it's all yours now.
